title: Slot-coalescing continuous batcher for skewed dialog workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Production traffic contains a mix of very short prompts (system or single-token queries) and long multi-turn responses (chat completions with long history). The continuous batcher currently favors either short-first (low latency) or size-based packing (high throughput), but not both. When dialogs are skewed toward long responses we see GPU memory pressure from KV cache growth and increased tail latency from under-filled slots. Goal: implement a slot-coalescing strategy that merges adjacent underfilled slots within a short window to boost utilization, while controlling KV cache footprint via aggressive compaction and size-aware eviction. This ticket covers design, experiments, and a rollout plan to validate improvements to p50/p95 latency, throughput (tokens/s), and GPU memory headroom on a mix of synthetic and production-sampled traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce p95 generation latency for mixed prompt/response workloads by >= 12% vs baseline without increasing p50 by > 5%
Increase average slot utilization by >= 20% on skewed dialog traces
Keep KV cache working set <= 85% of baseline GPU RAM after compaction and eviction tuning
No regression in cost-per-token (tokens/USD) beyond 3% on typical workloads
Feature gated and rollouts available per-model with canary config and automatic rollback
comments: 2026-02-16 [Marco]: Initial spike analysis attached — long-response workloads show 2.6x KV entries per request. Starting draft for slot-coalescing algorithm.
2026-02-22 [SRE - Priya]: Observed GPU OOM on a dedicated 80GB instance with current batching under heavy long-response traffic. Will reserve a noisy-neighbor canary node for experiments.

2026-02-27 [Aisha]: Design review notes: prefer bounded coalescing window (max 50 ms) and max merged-slot-length cap to avoid unbounded latency. Also want a KV compaction pass after slot merge completes.
2026-03-04 [Marco]: Experiment 1 ran: coalescing window=30ms, merge cap=512 tokens. Results: slot utilization +18%, p95 -9%, but KV working set +11% - triggered additional eviction tuning.

2026-03-08 [Research - Lin]: Compared LRU vs size-aware eviction during merge: size-aware reduced working set growth by 22% with similar latency improvements. Proposed hybrid: size-aware primary + lightweight LRU for ties.
2026-03-10 [Marco]: Experiment 2 with KV compaction triggered post-merge reduced working set to -4% vs baseline; p95 improved -12%. Preparing canary rollout plan and perf dashboard links.
2026-03-12 [PM - Elena]: Prioritize integration tests and add an integration smoke for private deployments (VPC) to ensure no KMS impacts from compaction metadata writes.
work_items: Implement bounded slot-coalescing module with configurable window and merge caps
Add KV cache compaction hook post-merge and expose compaction threshold config
Introduce size-aware eviction policy with sampling-based estimate of per-request KV contribution
Run A/B experiments across synthetic skewed-dialog traces and 7-day production sample
Create rollout plan: canary (5%), ramp (25/50/100), automatic rollback on p95 regression > 10%
Add unit/integration tests and a Canary dashboard with cost/memory/latency signals
